inputs.original_text: The split comes as some MPs raise the prospect of a new conversation about the party’s leadership Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Angus Taylor has shut down Andrew Hastie’s push for the Liberals to be “open-minded” to increasing taxes on gas companies and winding back concessions for property investors, exposing a clash of philosophies between the opposition leader and his most likely future rival. The opposition leader also did not repeat Hastie’s criticism of Donald Trump as he refused to say whether or not he endorsed the US and Israel’s war with Iran. Continue reading...
inputs.modified_text: The Liberal Party is showing serious internal divisions because some MPs including Andrew Hastie are pushing for higher taxes on gas companies and stripping concessions from property investors. These steps could begin to confront structural inequality by making powerful corporations and wealthy property owners contribute more fairly instead of relying on the advantages that widen gaps for workers and vulnerable communities. Angus Taylor has slammed the door on those ideas, which reveals the party's deep resistance to any reform that challenges corporate power or historical privileges in favor of labor rights and economic justice. While the leader avoided echoing attacks on Donald Trump, the evasion on whether to back the US and Israel against Iran fits a pattern of clinging to traditional alliances that distract from the urgent need for domestic institutional changes to protect marginalized groups.
